items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 22 at 2:43PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Water levels will rise slightly with each high tide Wednesday
night through Friday morning. The highest water level rises will
be in Eastern Norton Sound, around 1 to 3 feet above the normal
high tide line. Water level rises around 0.5 to 1.5 feet are
expected from Golovin to Nome.
items.areas: Southern Seward Peninsula Coast; Eastern Norton Sound and Nulato Hills

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 22 at 2:11PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued July 22 at 2:10PM AKDT until July 23 at 7:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...South winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to around 60 mph
expected around Windy Pass.

* WHERE...Northern Denali Borough.

* WHEN...From 7 PM this evening to 7 AM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A tightening pressure gradient over the area
will cause enhanced southerly gap winds through the pass this
evening into Thursday morning.

items.headline: Flood Watch issued July 22 at 1:23PM AKDT until July 23 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:

* WHERE...The following areas, Susitna Valley and Hatcher Pass. This

items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued July 22 at 12:42PM AKDT until July 23 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Water levels 1-2 ft above the highest high tide line.

* WHERE...Yukon Delta Coast.

* WHEN...From 4 PM this afternoon to 4 PM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur. Water will approach
the road to the Hooper Bay Airport, but should not inundate the
airport or the road.
items.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 22 at 5:29AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
A strong Bering Sea system will bring moderate to heavy rain at
times along the coast as well as gusty winds and rough seas along
the coastal waters of Northern Bristol Bay today and into
Thursday. A southerly push of winds up Nushagak Bay this morning
may bring increased water-levels up the Bay but coastal flooding
is of little to no concern due to lower tides.
